joints.role: the whole leg hangs on these six; the flange root is the frame's worst corner
joints.today: M5 heat-set insert in each flange end, pilot Ø6.4 x 11, its axis the build direction; 2.94 mm of wall each side in the 13 mm flange; 1.5 N m
reasons: fault tension 851 N an insert against an estimated 1500 N pull-out (SF 1.76), pulled across the layers
the assembly torque already preloads it to 1.00 x that pull-out
the flange's layer check: R3o 0.93 against 1.0 (flange root, inner face (x 95, y -65.1)), 6 mm past the inserts' pilots

options.insert: today; keep preload <= 0.5 x pull-out (750 N, 0.75 N m) and the fault load (851 N) opens the joint; spin-out is not measured
options.sleeved through-bolt: M5 8.8 through the flange's length and the web (76.8 mm of steel sleeve, Ø8 x Ø5.3), nut in a hex pocket on the web's leg face, head on the cheek / under the plate: preload 5112 N (5.1 N m) in steel, 6.0 x the fault tension; no insert, no creep in the clamp
options.threaded-rod tie: the same with M5 rod and two nuts where no head fits; no gain here (the cheek side takes a head)
options.captive nut: a hex nut in a side pocket near the flange end: the 2.9 mm walls either side of an 8 mm nut split the flange; rejected
options.through-bolt on the plastic: no sleeve: the bolt precompresses the flange along its length (across the layers, the root's peel direction), but the preload creeps away (see preload)

joints.why: D74: the leg's primary load path and an insert at 1.0 x its pull-out at assembly torque. The sleeve keeps the preload out of the plastic; the flange root is then judged without precompression (conservative).
joints.pr2: cad/fivebar.py frame_mounts(): 6 x Ø8.1 sleeve bores through the flange and web, an M5 hex pocket on the leg face; the Ø8.1 bore leaves 2.45 mm walls in the 13 mm flange, so the bolt line gets a local boss and the frame is re-run; the rig plate and the body cheek keep their Ø5.5 holes; screws M5 x ~90 (mcmaster-parts). Mass with a 6061 sleeve; a steel one adds 67 g more

joints.role: the motor's torque and the leg's out-of-plane moment into the link
joints.today: 8 x M5 x 40 into the tapped 6061 adapter, heads on 24.5 mm of PA6-CF (Ø8.5 heads, no washer); 1.5 N m puts 45.5 MPa under each head
reasons: the hub's edge lifts at 104 N m (at 1200 N a screw); R1 puts 114.6 and R3 188.6 N m on it
45.5 MPa under the heads against the 25 MPa sustained screen

options.insert: n/a (the receiver is the machined adapter)
options.sleeved through-bolt: a crush sleeve per screw keeps the preload, but then nothing clamps the printed face: the moment rocks the link on its sleeves; no
options.clamp ring: a 6061 ring Ø66 / Ø41 x 4 under all 8 heads (1911 mm2): 4000 N a screw is 16.7 MPa on the plastic, the face stays shut to about 347 N m (the edge-lift moment scales with the clamp); layers in compression
options.metal bushing: a machined hub insert: the adapter (D46) already is one; growing it is the fallback

joints.why: D74: the clamp spreads over the hub so the screws can carry a real preload while the plastic stays under the sustained screen and in compression across its layers. Re-torque after 24 h and after the first humid week.
joints.pr2: cad/fivebar.py upper_link(): a Ø66 / Ø41 x 4 recess at the counterbores' floor for the ring; HUB_PRELOAD_N to the ring preload in cad/leg_studies.py; the ring as a made-to-order part with the adapter

joints.role: holds each motor on the frame; the dowels carry its torque
joints.today: 10 x M4 x 20 12.9 into the RS-04 case (5 mm thread), heads on 15.6 mm of PA6-CF; no torque set (issue #116)
reasons: The plastic under the head sets it: 25 MPa on 22.6 mm2 is 565 N

options.insert: n/a (the receiver is the motor's case)
options.sleeved through-bolt: a steel crush sleeve Ø7 x Ø4.3 x 15.6 under each head: the torque is then set by the motor's thread, not the plastic, and creep cannot loosen it
options.clamp ring: one 6061 ring under the 10 heads: heavier and in the way of the counterbores; no

joints.why: D74: the motor's mount; today the plastic limits each screw to about 565 N. Coordinate with the RS-04 support work (issue #116) and its fit job before changing the frame's lug ring.
joints.pr2: recommended; held until issue #116's mounting stack is settled (its fit job prints this ring)

joints.role: the knee pin's moment into the upper link
joints.today: two DIN 179 sleeves pressed into the eye (already metal bushings), the shoulder screw clamped by the M10 nyloc
reasons: the eye stub's root: layer check E1 0.77 against 2.0 (the worst in the leg)
R3: 167.9 N m at the sleeves, 37.9 MPa on the eye (SF 1.06)

options.metal bushing: today's sleeves stay; the stub around them grows (diameter and root fillet) until its root passes, judged by the layer check
options.sleeved through-bolt: tie bolts through the stub into the link body (precompressing the root): they cross the sleeves' bore; no room at Ø40
options.metal eye: a machined 6061 eye block bolted to the link (the D46 pattern): the fallback if the stub cannot pass

joints.why: The bushing is right; its plastic seat is not. A rounder, larger stub lowers the root's peel; orientation does not help it (orientation screen).
joints.pr2: cad/fivebar.py: the stub's diameter and root fillet swept on the compute host; a 0.5 x 45 deg lead-in at the bed-face mouth; the outer sleeve 0.1-0.2 mm proud

joints.role: the inner races' clamp at each knee
joints.today: 5/8 in 6061 tube between the two 6301 inner races, the 10 kN knee clamp through it
reasons: its Ø15.9 face is under the 6301's da min 17.6 mm: the clamp bears on the inner race's corner radius

options.metal bushing: a steel spacer Ø18-19.4 x Ø12.1, faced to the measured web gap (+0 / +0.05)

joints.why: SKF's abutment rule; the same part count

joints.role: the wheel's load and out-of-plane moment between the two lower links

reasons: the wheel link's hub root: layer check R1w 0.7 against 1.2
the front link's apex ring: E1 0.71 against 2.0

options.printed, bigger: a root fillet at the Ø64 shoulder; the ring wall 6 -> 10-12 mm: lowest mass, may not reach 1.2
options.metal bushing: a turned 6061 hub (journal, shoulder, circlip groove) clamped through the foot by the wheel's 4 x M6 (their heads then bear on metal, which also fixes the foot's crushed-plastic clamp); about +120 g a leg
options.split apex collar: the front link's inner half-eye as a separate printed collar, through-bolted to the link: the link then prints flat, and the bolts precompress the ring's layers

joints.why: The hub root needs its peel stress x0.6 and the ring x0.4. Metal is certain and costs mass; printed is light and needs the FEA to show it.
joints.pr2: both swept on the compute host; the lighter one that passes is drawn

joints.today: 4 x M6 x 30 from inside the hub, heads on 20.8 mm of PA6-CF; 8 N m puts 150.4 MPa under each head
reasons: needs >= 1331 N a screw; a bare head holds 1108 N at 25 MPa

options.washer: a DIN 433 washer (fits inside the Ø48 bore): 1521 N, 1.14 x the need
options.metal bushing: the turned apex hub's floor under the heads (option 6): the clamp in metal

joints.pick: washer now; metal with the apex hub if chosen
joints.why: The BotWheel foot is the rig's; D69's 10 in hub motor replaces it (W1, W2).
joints.pr2: DIN 433 M6 washers under the heads; torque from the washer's plastic screen

joints.today: Ø16 x 40 52100 pins 23 mm into blind Ø16.1 holes, retaining compound; TPU 95A sleeves
reasons: the retaining compound: Henkel does not normally recommend LOCTITE 638 on plastics (stress cracking of thermoplastics), and the printed hole may close the gap it needs (fits)
joints.why: Pins in blind holes carry the stop's bending into 23 mm of plastic
joints.pr2: a 0.5 x 45 deg lead-in at the bed-face mouth; a structural epoxy in place of the anaerobic compound, its gap set from C1 (C1 also tries the compound with activator on a printed bore)

play.basis: ISO 286-2 tolerance grades (F7, f9, n6, m6); DIN 179 drill bushings: bore F7, outside n6 (catalog/hardware.json eye_sleeve tolerances); ISO 7379 shoulder screws: shoulder f9; ISO 5753-1 radial internal clearance, group N; radial play = half the diametral clearance; the motors' backlash is measured on the rig (B1)

impact.note: every R3 margin is the undamped cut onto the stops; the rig's bumper or the measured power-off damping (B1) divides the knee load by the ratio above

coupons.name: bore and press-fit gauge
coupons.prints: one block a variant (-0.1 / 0 / +0.1 mm), PA6-CF, the leg recipe, bores vertical as in the parts, half the mouths chamfered 0.5 x 45 deg on the bed face
coupons.features: a 6301 seat (12 mm deep, Ø31 shoulder), a DIN 179 sleeve bore 40 mm long, a Ø16.1 x 23 blind stop-pin hole, two Ø4.94 x 12 dowel holes, a 61812 seat segment (10 mm)
coupons.settles: PRINT_HOLE_ERR for this printer (the hole each fit is drawn at), the press force and the grip dry and after a humid week, elephant's foot at the mouths, retaining compound on printed bores

coupons.name: insert pull-out and spin-out in the real wall (B4a)
coupons.prints: three flange-end slices of the hip frame (13 mm flange, Ø14 boss, the real 2.94 mm walls), printed as the frame (insert axis vertical)
coupons.features: the M5 insert at the frame's depth; a Ø15 bearing washer under the puller
coupons.settles: the insert's pull-out across the layers in this wall (the 1500 N estimate) and its spin-out torque: the numbers the insert option is judged on, kept even if the mount goes to through-bolts (other leg and body inserts)

coupons.name: sleeved through-bolt joint, against the plastic clamp
coupons.prints: four 13 x 40 x 60 flange blocks, layers across the bolt as in the frame
coupons.features: two with an Ø8.1 bore and a steel sleeve flush, two with an Ø5.5 bore (bolt on the plastic, a Ø15 washer); M5 8.8 through the B4 load cell
coupons.settles: preload kept over 30 min, 24 h, 7 days and a humid week, sleeved against plain; the creep step the preload table screens; the re-torque schedule

coupons.name: boss-root layer coupon (the knee eye's stub)
coupons.prints: the upper link's knee end, cut 40 mm back from the knee, printed as the link (stub up); two today, two with the PR 2 stub
coupons.features: the two DIN 179 sleeves and a Ø12 pin standing 46 mm out (the knee's lever), loaded sideways in the press cage
coupons.settles: the load at which the stub's root peels (or the arm breaks) against the FEA's prediction for the same coupon: calibrates S_z and the unmeasured interlayer shear S_s the layer check assumes
